articles.title: Suzlon Energy Q2 FY27 Results: Revenue Up 26%, Order Book Crosses 6 GW
articles.description: Suzlon Energy Limited, one of India’s leading renewable energy companies and wind turbine manufacturers, has reported a robust 26% year-on-year increase in consolidated revenue from operations to ₹4,869 crore for the second quarter of financial year 2026–27, ended September 30, 2026. The company’s latest financial results highlight growing demand for wind energy solutions, higher turbine deliveries, stronger commissioning activity and an expanding order pipeline. However, despite the impressive operational performance, profitability remained under pressure due to rising input costs, commodity-price fluctuations, foreign-exchange volatility and changing project execution requirements. Suzlon’s consolidated net profit stood at approximately ₹394 crore, compared with the reported ₹1,279 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. At first glance, this represents a sharp decline of approximately 69%. However, the comparison requires important clarification. The corresponding quarter last year included a deferred-tax asset benefit of approximately ₹891 crore, which significantly increased reported profitability. Excluding this exceptional tax benefit, Suzlon’s comparable net profit increased marginally by approximately 1.3%, from ₹389 crore to ₹394 crore. The September 2026 quarter therefore presents a picture of expanding business operations and improving execution capabilities, alongside a continuing challenge in translating higher revenue into stronger operating margins. Suzlon Energy Q2 FY27: Key Financial Highlights Suzlon’s quarterly performance reflects significant expansion in business volumes, although its earnings profile remains mixed. On a sequential basis, Suzlon reported encouraging improvements. Revenue increased approximately 27% from ₹3,819 crore in the April–June 2026 quarter, while net profit rose around 29% from ₹305 crore. EBITDA also improved sequentially by approximately 21%, from ₹595 crore to ₹720 crore. Nevertheless, the year-on-year reduction in EBITDA margin from 18.6% to 14.8% remains a key financial development that investors, analysts and industry stakeholders will be closely monitoring. Record 710 MW Deliveries Signal Improving Execution Capabilities One of the most encouraging aspects of Suzlon’s second-quarter performance was its record wind turbine delivery volume. The company delivered 710 megawatts (MW) of wind turbine capacity during the quarter, representing an increase of approximately 26% from 565 MW in the corresponding period last year. Compared with the preceding quarter’s deliveries of approximately 506 MW, execution improved by around 40%. Wind turbine commissioning also showed significant acceleration, reaching 454 MW during the September quarter. This represented a year-on-year increase of approximately 196%. These numbers are particularly relevant because the wind energy industry often encounters project execution challenges involving land availability, transportation of large equipment, grid connectivity, construction schedules and weather-related interruptions. Higher delivery volumes and stronger commissioning activity suggest progress in converting confirmed orders into operational renewable-energy assets. For the first half of FY27, Suzlon reported total turbine deliveries of approximately 1,217 MW, compared with 1,009 MW in the corresponding period last year. The company’s commissioning volume for the six-month period reached approximately 723 MW. Suzlon also reported a pipeline of around 1,295 MW of erected turbines awaiting commissioning, providing visibility into future commissioning opportunities, subject to site readiness and other execution conditions. Order Book Crosses 6 GW, Providing Business Visibility Suzlon’s order book remained one of the strongest indicators of its growth potential. As of September 30, 2026, the company’s outstanding order book stood at approximately 6,009 MW, compared with 5,697 MW at the end of March 2026. The company secured more than 1.5 GW of new order intake during the first half of FY27. The order pipeline is supported by demand from commercial and industrial enterprises, public sector organisations, captive power users and renewable-energy developers. Suzlon has indicated that approximately 78% of its order book is linked to public sector and commercial and industrial customer categories. Such diversification is important because India’s energy transition is no longer dependent exclusively on large utility-scale renewable-energy projects. Corporate decarbonisation commitments, captive renewable-energy procurement, energy-cost optimisation and the growing popularity of hybrid renewable-energy projects are helping broaden the addressable market for wind power. The company’s order book offers substantial revenue visibility, although the eventual financial contribution will depend on execution schedules, contract conditions, project commissioning and cost management. Profitability Challenge: Why Did EBITDA Margins Decline? Despite impressive revenue growth, Suzlon’s EBITDA remained almost unchanged at approximately ₹720 crore, compared with ₹721 crore during the previous year’s corresponding quarter. Consequently, its EBITDA margin contracted to 14.8% from 18.6%. The reduction of approximately 3.8 percentage points indicates that operating expenses increased faster than revenue. According to the company’s management commentary, changes in customer mix, the scope of project contracts, commodity-price volatility and foreign-exchange fluctuations contributed to the decline in profitability. Suzlon has increasingly expanded its engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) offerings, under which the company undertakes broader project responsibilities beyond supplying wind turbines. While this strategy can increase the value of contracts and potentially deepen customer relationships, EPC projects can carry additional procurement, construction and execution expenses. EPC-related work accounted for approximately 38% of Suzlon’s order book, reflecting the growing significance of integrated project solutions in its business model. The company also incurred additional expenses associated with its organisational expansion and Suzlon 2.0 transformation initiatives. Management has indicated that certain expenses could moderate in subsequent quarters, while improvements in project execution and operating leverage may support profitability. However, sustainable margin recovery will depend on managing costs effectively as delivery volumes continue to rise. Renewable Energy Solutions Business Records Strong Growth Suzlon’s Renewable Energy Solutions segment, representing its core wind energy equipment and project business, recorded revenue of approximately ₹4,212 crore during Q2 FY27. This was an increase of nearly 30% from ₹3,241 crore during the same quarter last year. However, segment profitability declined despite higher sales. The segment result decreased to approximately ₹371 crore from ₹478 crore in Q2 FY26, highlighting the impact of cost pressures and changes in the business mix. This development reinforces an important industry reality: increasing equipment deliveries does not automatically translate into proportionate earnings growth. For capital-intensive renewable-energy manufacturers, maintaining procurement efficiency, controlling project execution costs and protecting margins against changes in raw-material prices remain crucial. Asset Management Services Provide Stability While the core wind turbine business experienced margin pressure, Suzlon’s Renewable Energy Asset Management Services segment delivered encouraging performance. The segment recorded revenue of approximately ₹640 crore, compared with ₹575 crore in the previous year’s corresponding quarter. Its segment result increased from approximately ₹145 crore to ₹220 crore. This business provides operations, maintenance and asset management services for renewable-energy installations. Such services can offer relatively recurring revenue streams compared with equipment manufacturing, where revenues depend on new project execution and delivery schedules. For Suzlon, expanding its renewable-energy asset management activities could strengthen long-term customer relationships and provide additional earnings diversification. Balance Sheet Strengthens; Net Worth Crosses ₹10,000 Crore Suzlon’s financial position remains an important element of its business transformation. The company reported consolidated net worth of approximately ₹10,277 crore as of September 2026, crossing the ₹10,000 crore milestone. Its reported net cash position stood at approximately ₹2,048 crore. CRISIL upgraded the company’s long-term credit rating to AA-/Stable, reflecting an improved assessment of its credit profile. A stronger balance sheet can support investments in manufacturing facilities, technology development, supply-chain expansion and project execution capabilities. However, the company’s working-capital requirements remain an area requiring attention. Operating cash flow was negative during the first half of FY27, reflecting pressure from inventory accumulation and receivables associated with project execution. For a company operating in a capital-intensive industry, the conversion of revenue and accounting profits into operating cash flow remains an essential measure of financial sustainability. What Suzlon Management Says About the Business Outlook Suzlon Group Chief Executive Officer Ajay Kapur has emphasised the company’s improving execution performance, highlighting record second-quarter deliveries and stronger commissioning activity. Management has also pointed to its substantial order book and new business wins as indicators of continuing demand for the company’s wind energy solutions. Chief Financial Officer Rahul Jain has acknowledged the impact of commodity and currency volatility while underscoring the company’s focus on manufacturing capabilities, operational discipline, cash flow and capital allocation. Following the quarterly results, management indicated a more cautious outlook for FY27 EBITDA margins, with expectations in the region of 15–16%, compared with an earlier reference level of around 17%. The company expects higher operating volumes during the second half of the financial year to potentially provide operating leverage. Nevertheless, the pace of margin recovery will depend on commodity costs, customer and project mix, execution efficiency and working-capital management. What Suzlon’s Growth Means for Indian MSMEs and the Wind Energy Supply Chain Beyond its impact on shareholders, Suzlon’s business expansion carries wider implications for India’s manufacturing ecosystem, particularly micro, small and medium enterprises. The wind energy industry depends on a complex network of engineering, manufacturing, fabrication, electrical equipment, transportation, construction and maintenance service providers. Growing wind turbine manufacturing and project commissioning activity could create business opportunities for MSMEs engaged in precision engineering, metal fabrication, forgings, industrial components, electrical systems, logistics, specialised transportation and technical maintenance services. India’s expanding renewable-energy ecosystem could also encourage greater localisation of components and improve opportunities for domestic industrial suppliers. For smaller manufacturers, participation in the wind energy supply chain may provide access to long-term industrial relationships and opportunities to upgrade technical capabilities. However, these opportunities should not be confused with confirmed procurement contracts or guaranteed business growth. MSME suppliers seeking to participate in this sector must address strict product-quality standards, certification requirements, delivery schedules, competitive pricing and working-capital management. Large renewable-energy projects often involve extended execution cycles, making timely payments and adequate financial planning particularly important for smaller suppliers. The increasing complexity of integrated wind-energy projects could create demand for specialised engineering and service providers capable of meeting large project developers’ operational requirements. For the Indian MSME ecosystem, sustained renewable-energy capacity expansion can therefore support industrial diversification, technology adoption and new supply-chain opportunities, provided smaller enterprises are able to compete effectively. India’s Wind Energy Transition: Growth Opportunities and Challenges India’s renewable-energy transition is creating a broader market for wind power as companies, utilities and policymakers seek cleaner and more diversified sources of electricity. Wind energy is particularly relevant to the expansion of renewable-energy portfolios because generation patterns can complement solar power in certain locations and seasons. Growing interest in wind-solar hybrid projects, commercial and industrial renewable-energy procurement and round-the-clock clean-power solutions could support demand for wind turbine equipment and associated infrastructure. At the same time, India’s wind energy sector must contend with land availability, transmission infrastructure, grid integration, financing conditions and execution-related complexities. Manufacturers such as Suzlon will need to balance market-share growth with profitability, timely project delivery and sustainable capital deployment. The company’s latest performance illustrates both sides of this evolving business environment: rising demand and improving execution on one hand, and greater cost and working-capital pressures on the other. Market Outlook: Analysts Focus on Profit Margins and Cash Flow Following Suzlon’s quarterly earnings announcement, brokerage assessments reflected differing expectations about its future profitability and valuation. UBS retained its Buy rating but reduced its target price from ₹66 to ₹58, reflecting revised earnings expectations. Nuvama Institutional Equities maintained its Hold rating while lowering its target price from ₹51 to ₹41, citing weaker-than-expected margins and profitability pressures. These targets reflect the respective brokerages’ independent research assumptions and do not constitute assured future prices or recommendations by SMEStreet. The company’s earnings performance demonstrates why revenue growth, order book strength and turbine deliveries need to be evaluated alongside operating margins, cash flow and project profitability. What to Watch in Suzlon’s Upcoming Quarters Several developments will be important in assessing Suzlon’s progress over the remainder of FY27. First, operating-margin recovery. The company’s ability to improve EBITDA margins will indicate whether expanding turbine deliveries can generate stronger financial returns. Second, order execution. Converting its 6 GW-plus order book into completed deliveries and commissioned projects will remain fundamental to sustaining revenue growth. Third, cash-flow improvement. Reducing working-capital pressure and improving operating cash generation could strengthen financial flexibility. Fourth, manufacturing and supply-chain efficiency. The ability to manage commodity costs, procurement risks and EPC-related expenses will influence overall profitability. Fifth, new business opportunities. Further order inflows from corporate customers, public sector enterprises and renewable-energy developers could help sustain the company’s medium-term growth visibility. SMEStreet Perspective: Strong Business Momentum, but Profitability Remains the Real Test Suzlon Energy’s second-quarter FY27 performance reflects meaningful progress in the company’s operating capabilities. Record turbine deliveries, improving commissioning activity, a substantial order book and stronger balance-sheet indicators provide an encouraging foundation for continued business expansion. However, the contraction in EBITDA margins and negative operating cash flow during the first half of the financial year cannot be overlooked. The results also demonstrate the importance of distinguishing between reported profit and underlying operating performance. The substantial year-on-year decline in reported net profit was primarily influenced by the previous year’s exceptional deferred-tax benefit, rather than an equivalent deterioration in current-quarter operating earnings. Nevertheless, flat EBITDA despite higher revenue indicates genuine pressure on operating profitability. For India’s renewable-energy sector, Suzlon’s growth reflects an expanding industrial opportunity with potential benefits for equipment manufacturers, infrastructure developers and MSME supply-chain participants. The next phase of the company’s performance will depend not merely on how many turbines it sells, but on how efficiently it executes projects, protects margins and converts its expanding order book into sustainable profitability and cash flows. For Suzlon, the central business challenge ahead is to ensure that strong operational growth translates into equally convincing financial performance. articles.title: India News | DGHS Medical Procurement Scam: 'Tender Files Destroyed Intentionally,' Rs 839 Crores Paid to 5 Beneficiary Companies, Claims ACB
articles.description: Get latest articles and stories on India at LatestLY. The Anti-Corruption Branch (ACB) on Thursday alleged that tender files were intentionally destroyed by the accused persons in the DGHS medical procurement case. In its chargesheet, ACB also claimed that bills were not prepared through GeM and payment of Rs 839 crore was made to five beneficiary companies.

articles.title: GeM Cuts Transaction Charges to 0.30%, Raises Exemption Threshold to ₹10 Lakh for MSEs
